title: A King Promises to Rule Honestly
overview: A king, traditionally David, vows to live with integrity in his own home and to keep slanderers, the proud, the deceitful and the wicked away from his court and city.

parts.label: A song of love and justice (vv. 1-2a)
parts.note: The king opens by praising God for both kindness and fairness, and he may also be promising to show those same two qualities as a ruler. His question asking when God will come to him is unclear; it may express a longing for God's presence, and scholars are unsure what event, if any, lies behind it.

parts.label: Integrity starts at home (vv. 2b-4)
parts.note: Before he speaks about the wider land, he promises to live honestly in his own household, where no crowd is watching. He refuses to look approvingly on anything shameful and wants nothing to do with people whose hearts are twisted or who turn away from what is right.

parts.label: Who will serve in his court (vv. 5-7)
parts.note: Royal courts were full of people seeking favor through gossip, flattery and lies, so he vows to shut out secret slanderers, the arrogant and the deceitful. Instead, he will look for faithful, honest people to live near him and serve him.

parts.label: Daily justice in the city (v. 8)
parts.note: Kings often heard legal cases in the morning, so his vow to act against the wicked day after day likely means steady, ongoing judgment rather than one dramatic purge. The language of silencing and cutting off wrongdoers is harsh, and it reflects a king's real power to punish and remove them from Jerusalem, called here the city of the LORD.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether this psalm is mainly a practical model for any leader or household, or chiefly a picture of the ideal king, which many Christians read as fulfilled only in Jesus.
think: Is it harder to be the person you want to be in public, or at home where fewer people see you?
